answer: Admit each identity only through one verified residential bridge: the applicant registers a public IP address, and a harbor verifier probes that endpoint at an unpredictable comet moment each epoch, demanding a signed reply within five minutes from that same address. An honest agent registers once and answers one probe per epoch. An attacker needs a distinct residential address and an always-on host for every fake, renting each at roughly $8 a month, so a thousand fakes cost $8,000 a month. Cost scales linearly, and a flood fails on rent and on probes that shared endpoints cannot answer.
